problems.problem: Describe the set of points $P(x, y)$ whose distance to $A(3, 0)$ is twice their distance to $O(0, 0)$.
Prove that for $0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$ $$\sin x + \tan x > 2x.$$
A right triangle has perimeter $60$, and the altitude to the hypotenuse has length $12$. Determine the lengths of the sides.
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ be arbitrary real numbers. Prove that if $$a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = ab + bc + cd + da,$$ then $a = b = c = d$.
Show that no matter how $15$ points are placed within a circle of radius $2$ (boundary included), there exists a circle of radius $1$ (boundary included) containing at least three of the $15$ points.

A man in a rowing boat is at the point $A$, at a distance of $2$ kilometres from a straight stretch of coast. By first rowing to a point $P$ on the coast and then walking along the coast, he reaches the point $B$, which lies at a distance of $5$ kilometres from $C$, the point on the coast nearest to $A$. The man's rowing speed is $3$ kilometres per hour, and his walking speed is $5$ kilometres per hour. Determine where $P$ should be placed between $C$ and $B$ so that the man gets from $A$ to $B$ in the shortest possible time.

In a right triangle, $a$ and $b$ denote the lengths of the two legs. A circle with radius $r$ has its centre on the hypotenuse and touches both legs. Show that $$\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{r}.$$
Let $x$ and $y$ be positive numbers with $x + y = 1$. Show that $$\left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)\left(1 + \frac{1}{y}\right) \ge 9.$$

Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ denote the side lengths and $m_a$, $m_b$ and $m_c$ the lengths of the medians of an arbitrary triangle. Show that $$\frac{3}{4} < \frac{m_a + m_b + m_c}{a + b + c} < 1.$$ Show furthermore that there is no narrower interval which, for every triangle, contains the quantity $$\frac{m_a + m_b + m_c}{a + b + c}.$$

A hat contains $1992$ slips of paper with all the numbers from $1$ to $1992$. Two slips are drawn at random simultaneously; the difference between the numbers on the two slips is written on a new slip, which is put into the hat, while the two drawn slips are discarded. This continues until only one slip is left in the hat. Show that the number on this slip is even.

Three friends $A$, $B$ and $C$ together have $120$ kroner. First $A$ gives $B$ as much money as $B$ already has. Then $B$ gives $C$ as much money as $C$ already has. Finally $C$ gives $A$ as much money as $A$ now has. After these transactions $A$, $B$ and $C$ have equal amounts of money. How much money did each of the three friends have originally?

A rectangular piece of paper has side lengths $12$ and $15$. A corner is folded over as shown in the figure. Determine the area of the grey triangle.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1993_p2_fig.png
Determine all real solutions $(x, y)$ of the system of equations $$x^2 + y^2 = 1, \qquad x^6 + y^6 = \frac{7}{16}.$$

In triangle $ABC$ the points $D$, $E$ and $F$ cut off one third of the respective sides. Show that the sum of the areas of the three grey triangles is equal to the area of the middle triangle.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1993_p4_fig.png

A cardboard box contains a large number of loose socks. Some of the socks are red; the others are blue. It is given that the total number of socks does not exceed $1993$. Furthermore, it is given that the probability of drawing two socks of the same colour, when two socks are drawn at random from the box, is $\frac{1}{2}$. According to this information, what is the largest number of red socks that can be in the box?

A wine glass with a cross-section as shown has the property that an orange shaped like a ball of radius $3$ cm can just be placed in the glass without sticking out above the glass. Determine the height $h$ of the glass.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1994_p1_fig.png

A train covers a certain distance at a constant speed. If the speed is increased by $10$ kilometres per hour, the trip can be made $40$ minutes faster. If, on the other hand, the speed is decreased by $10$ kilometres per hour, the trip takes $1$ hour longer. How long is the distance covered?
The cubic polynomial $P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 3x - 5$ has the three roots $a$, $b$ and $c$. Give a cubic polynomial with the roots $\frac{1}{a}$, $\frac{1}{b}$ and $\frac{1}{c}$.
In a right triangle in which all side lengths are integers, one leg has length $1994$. Determine the length of the hypotenuse.
In an isosceles right triangle both legs have length $1$. Find the length of the shortest line segment that divides the triangle into two figures of equal area, and give the position of this segment.

A trapezoid has side lengths as shown in the figure (the sides of lengths $11$ and $36$ are parallel). Compute the area of the trapezoid.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1995_p1_fig.png
Find all sets of five consecutive integers with the property that the sum of the squares of the first three numbers equals the sum of the squares of the last two.
From the vertex $C$ of triangle $ABC$ a straight line is drawn which bisects the median from $A$. In what ratio does this line divide the side $AB$?
Solve the equation $$(2^x - 4)^3 + (4^x - 2)^3 = (4^x + 2^x - 6)^3,$$ where $x$ is a real number.
Six circles are given in the plane such that none of the circles contains the centre of another. Show that there is no point lying in all the circles.

In triangle $ABC$ the angle $C$ is right, and the two legs both have length $1$. For a given choice of the point $P$ on the leg $BC$, the point $Q$ is placed on the hypotenuse and the point $R$ on the other leg such that $PQ$ is parallel to $AC$ and $QR$ is parallel to $BC$. In this way the triangle is divided into three parts. Determine the positions of the point $P$ for which the rectangular part has a larger area than each of the other two parts.
Determine all triples of real numbers $(x, y, z)$ satisfying the system of equations $$xy = z, \qquad xz = y, \qquad yz = x.$$

This year's gift idea from BabyMath consists of a series of nine coloured plastic containers of decreasing size, alternately shaped like a cube and a sphere. All containers can be opened and closed with a practical hinge, and each container can exactly hold the next one in the series. The largest and the smallest containers are both cubes. Determine the ratio between the edge lengths of these two cubes.
About a natural number $n$ it is given that the number $n^2$ has $7$ as its second-to-last digit. What is the last digit of $n^2$?

In a ballroom, seven gentlemen $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, $F$ and $G$ sit directly opposite seven ladies $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$, $f$ and $g$, in random order. When the gentlemen rise and cross the dance floor to bow to their respective ladies, somebody notices that at least two of the gentlemen cover equally long distances. Will this always be the case? The figure shows an example. In the example, $|Bb| = |Ee|$ and $|Dd| = |Cc|$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1996_p5_fig.png
Let $n = 123456789101112\ldots998999$ be the natural number obtained by writing the natural numbers from $1$ to $999$ one after another. What is digit number $1997$ of $n$?

Two squares, both with side length $1$, are placed so that one of them has a vertex at the centre of the other. Determine the area of the grey region.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1997_p2_fig.png

In pentagon $ABCDE$ the angles $A$ and $C$ are right, and the sides satisfy $|AB| = 4$, $|BC| = 5$, $|CD| = 10$, $|DE| = 6$. Furthermore, the point $C'$, obtained by reflecting $C$ in the line $BD$, lies on the segment $AE$. Find the angle $E$.
Find all pairs $(x, y)$ of natural numbers satisfying the equation $$x^2 - xy + 2x - 3y = 1997.$$

A $7 \times 7$ square is cut into pieces of the following types (type (a) and type (b)):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1997_p5_fig.png

Show that exactly one of the pieces is of type (b).

In the figure shown, the small circles have radius $1$. Compute the area of the grey part of the figure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1998_p1_fig.png
For every real number $m$ the equation $$x^2 + (m-2)x - (m+3) = 0$$ has two solutions, denoted $x_1$ and $x_2$. Determine $m$ such that $x_1^2 + x_2^2$ is as small as possible.

On three parallel lines, with distances as given in the figure, lie the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ such that the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square. Find the area of this square.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_1998_p3_fig.png
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive real numbers with $a + b = 1$. Show that $$\left(a + \frac{1}{a}\right)^2 + \left(b + \frac{1}{b}\right)^2 \ge \frac{25}{2}.$$

A nice fruit arrangement on a large round platter is bordered with strawberries. Between $100$ and $200$ berries have been used for this border. A greedy child first eats one of the strawberries and then starts walking round and round the platter, eating strawberries in the following way: when she has eaten a berry, she leaves the next one, then eats the next one, leaves the next one, and so on. She continues in this way until only a single strawberry is left. This berry is the one that lay immediately after the very first one she ate. How many berries were there originally?

In a coordinate system, a circle with radius $7$ and centre on the $y$-axis is placed inside the parabola with equation $y = x^2$, so that it just touches the parabola at two points. Determine the coordinates of the centre of the circle.

A fisherman has caught a number of fish. The three heaviest together make up $35\%$ of the total weight of the catch. He sells them. Afterwards, the three lightest together make up $\frac{5}{13}$ of the weight of the rest. How many fish did he catch?
A function $f$ satisfies $$f(x) + x f(1-x) = x$$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine the number $f(2)$. Determine a formula for $f$.

Nanna and Sofie are moving in the same direction along two parallel paths which are $200$ metres apart. Nanna's speed is $3$ metres per second, Sofie's only $1$ metre per second. A tall cylindrical building with a diameter of $100$ metres is placed midway between the two paths. At the moment when the building first blocks the line of sight between the girls, their mutual distance is $200$ metres. How long does it take before the two girls can see each other again?
Is there a number whose digits are all $1$'s and which is divisible by $1999$?

The quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square with side length $1$, and the points $E$, $F$, $G$ and $H$ are the midpoints of the sides. Determine the area of the quadrilateral $PQRS$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2000_p1_fig.png

In a glass with vertical rectangular side faces and with a regular hexagon as bottom and lid, three equal balls can just be placed on top of each other so that each of the balls touches all the sides of the glass. The volume of the glass is $108\text{ cm}^3$. What is the side length of the base?

A GEORG MOHR cube is a cube on whose six faces the letters G, E, O, R, M and H are printed, respectively. Peter has nine identical GEORG MOHR cubes. Is it possible to stack them on top of each other into a tower which, on each of its four sides, shows the letters G E O R G M O H R in some order?

A rectangular floor is covered by a number of equally large square tiles. The tiles along the edge are red, and the rest are white. There are equally many red and white tiles. How many tiles can there be?
Determine all possible values of $x + \frac{1}{x}$, where the real number $x$ satisfies the equation $$x^4 + 5x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x + 1 = 0,$$ and solve this equation.

The GEORG MOHR game uses a piece, a GEORG MOHR die (i.e. a die whose six faces show the letters G, E, O, R, M and H) and a game board (the circle on the left is the starting field with the piece, and the circled R on the right is the final field):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2001_p1_fig.png

With each throw one moves forward to the first following field with the letter shown by the die; if it is not possible to move forward, one stays where one is. Peter plays the GEORG MOHR game. Determine the probability that he completes the game in two throws.
Is there a natural number $n$ such that the number $n!$ ends in exactly $11$ zeros? (Here $n!$ denotes the number $1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdots (n-1) \cdot n$.)
In the square $ABCD$ with side length $2$, $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $P$ is a point on $DC$. Determine the smallest value of $|AP| + |PM|$.
Show that every number of the form $$4444\ldots44 - 88\ldots8,$$ where there are twice as many $4$'s as $8$'s, is a perfect square.
Can an equilateral triangle be placed inside a square so that the area of the triangle is more than $\frac{9}{20}$ of the area of the square?

From an interior point of a rectangle, line segments are drawn to the midpoints of the four sides. This creates four regions (polygons) with areas $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ (see the figure). Prove that $a + c = b + d$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2002_p1_fig.png
Prove that for every integer $n$ greater than $5$, a square can be divided into $n$ squares.
Two positive integers have the sum $2002$. Can $2002$ divide the product of the two numbers?
In triangle $ABC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$ and $|AC| = |BC|$. Furthermore, $M$ is an interior point of the triangle such that $|MC| = 1$, $|MA| = 2$ and $|MB| = \sqrt{2}$. Compute $|AB|$.

Homer Grog has written the numbers $1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17$ on ten slips of paper, one number on each slip. He arranges the slips in a circle and tries to make the largest sum $S$ of the numbers on three consecutive slips as small as possible. What is the smallest value $S$ can take?
In a right triangle, the sum $a + b$ of the lengths of the legs is $24$, while the altitude $h_c$ to the hypotenuse $c$ has length $7$. Determine the length of the hypotenuse.
Solve in the real numbers the equation $$x^5 + \lfloor x \rfloor = 20,$$ where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $x$.
Determine the integers $n$ for which $$|2n^2 + 9n + 4|$$ is a prime.

Georg and his mother love pizza. They buy a pizza shaped like an equilateral triangle. Georg demands to be allowed to divide the pizza with a straight cut and then to choose first. His mother reluctantly accepts, but she wants to point out a point in the pizza through which the cut must pass. Determine the largest fraction of the pizza that the mother can be sure to get with this procedure.

For which natural numbers $n \ge 2$ can the numbers from $1$ to $16$ be placed in a square $4 \times 4$ array so that the four row sums and the four column sums are all mutually different and divisible by $n$?

The rectangle $ABCD$ is twice as wide as it is high, and the rectangle $EFCG$ is twice as high as it is wide. The point $E$ lies on the diagonal $BD$. What fraction of the area of the large rectangle is the area of the small rectangle?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2004_p1_fig.png
Show that if $a$ and $b$ are integers and $a^2 + b^2 + 9ab$ is divisible by $11$, then $a^2 - b^2$ is divisible by $11$.

The digits from $1$ to $9$ are placed in the figure below, one digit in each square. The sum of the three numbers placed in the same horizontal or vertical line is $13$. Show that the number in the marked place is $4$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2004_p3_fig.png
Find all triples $(x, y, z)$ of real numbers satisfying $$x^3 - y^2 = z^2 - x, \qquad y^3 - z^2 = x^2 - y, \qquad z^3 - x^2 = y^2 - z.$$

Determine for which natural numbers $n$ a $2n \times 2n$ board can be covered by non-overlapping L-pieces. An L-piece covers four squares and is shaped like the letter L. The piece may be rotated and reflected as desired.

The figure comes from a cut-out sheet. When the side faces are folded up along the dashed lines, a (non-equilateral) pyramid with a square base is formed. Compute the area of the base.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2005_p1_fig.png
Determine, for every positive real number $a$, the number of solutions $(x, y)$ of the system of equations $$|x| + |y| = 1, \qquad x^2 + y^2 = a,$$ where $x$ and $y$ are real numbers.

The point $P$ lies inside $\triangle ABC$ such that $\triangle BPC$ is isosceles and the angle at $P$ is right. Furthermore, $\triangle BAN$ and $\triangle CAM$ are both isosceles with a right angle at $A$, and both lie outside $\triangle ABC$. Show that $\triangle MNP$ is isosceles and right-angled.

Fourteen students each write an integer on the blackboard. When they later meet their mathematics teacher Homer Grog, they tell him that no matter which number they erased from the blackboard, the remaining numbers could be divided into three groups with the same sum. They also tell him that the numbers on the blackboard were integers. Is it now possible for Homer Grog to determine which numbers the students wrote on the blackboard?

For which real numbers $p$ does the system of equations $$x_1^4 + \frac{1}{x_1^2} = p x_2, \quad x_2^4 + \frac{1}{x_2^2} = p x_3, \quad \dots, \quad x_{2004}^4 + \frac{1}{x_{2004}^2} = p x_{2005}, \quad x_{2005}^4 + \frac{1}{x_{2005}^2} = p x_1$$ have exactly one solution $(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2005})$, where $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{2005}$ are real numbers?

The star shown is symmetric with respect to each of the six diagonals shown. All segments from the points $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_6$ to the centre of the star have length $1$, and all the angles shown at $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_6$ are right angles. Determine the area of the star.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2006_p1_fig.png
Determine all triples of real numbers $(x, y, z)$ satisfying $$x + y = 2 \quad \text{and} \quad xy - z^2 = 1.$$

A natural number $n$, which is at most $500$, has the property that when a number $m$ is chosen at random among the numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, 499, 500$, the probability that $m$ divides $n$ is $\frac{1}{100}$. Determine the largest possible value of $n$.

Ten distinct numbers are to be chosen from the numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, 2006$. Show that ten distinct numbers with sum greater than $10039$ can be chosen in more ways than ten distinct numbers with sum less than $10030$.

Consider an acute triangle $ABC$. The altitude from $A$ is $AD$, the altitude from $D$ in triangle $ABD$ is $DE$, and the altitude from $D$ in triangle $ACD$ is $DF$.

(a) Prove that the triangles $ABC$ and $AFE$ are similar.

(b) Prove that the segment $EF$ and the corresponding segments formed starting from the vertices $B$ and $C$ all have the same length.

In a regular decagon, the triangle $ABC$ lies as shown in the figure. What fraction of the area of the whole decagon is the area of the triangle? The answer should be written as a fraction whose numerator and denominator are integers.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2007_p1_fig.png
What is the last digit of the number $2007^{2007}$?

A cunning dragon guards a princess. To overcome the dragon and win the princess, one must solve the following task: the dragon has placed the numbers $1$–$8$ in some of the fields of the hall of pillars (see the figure). One must place the numbers $9$–$36$ in the remaining fields oneself. The numbers $1$–$36$ must be placed so that every walk that starts by entering from either the south or the west and ends by leaving towards either the north or the east passes through at least one number from the $5$ times table. (In the figure, north, south, east and west are indicated by N, S, E and W.)

Georg wants to win the princess. Can it be done?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2007_p3_fig.png

The figure shows an angle of $60^\circ$ in which $2007$ numbered circles lie (only the first $3$ are shown in the figure). The circles are numbered by size. The circles are tangent to the arms of the angle and to each other as shown in the figure. Circle number $1$ has radius $1$.

Determine the radius of circle number $2007$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2007_p4_fig.png

The numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ are determined by $a_0 = 0$ and $$a_n = \begin{cases} 1 + a_{n-1} & \text{if } n \text{ is positive and odd,} \\ 3a_{n/2} & \text{if } n \text{ is positive and even.} \end{cases}$$ How many of these numbers are less than $2007$?

Denmark has played a football international against Georgia. The match ended $5$–$5$, and between the first and the last goal the match was never level at any time. Neither country scored three goals in a row, and Denmark scored the sixth goal.

Can one determine from this information which country scored the fifth goal?
Three integers $p$, $q$ and $r$ satisfy $p + q^2 = r^2$. Show that $6$ divides $pqr$.

The numbers from $1$ to $500$ are written on the board. Two players $A$ and $B$ alternately erase one number at a time, and $A$ erases the first number. If the sum of the last two numbers on the board is divisible by $3$, $B$ wins; otherwise $A$ wins.

Which player can devise a strategy that guarantees this player victory?

In triangle $ABC$, $|AB| = 2$, $|AC| = 6$ and $\angle A = 120^\circ$. The bisector of angle $A$ meets the side $BC$ at the point $D$.

Determine the length of $AD$. The answer should be given as a fraction with integers in the numerator and denominator.

For each positive integer $n$, a new number $t_n$ is formed from the numbers $2^n$ and $5^n$, consisting of the digits of $2^n$ followed by the digits of $5^n$. For example, $t_4 = 16625$.

How many digits does the number $t_{2008}$ have?

In the figure, triangle $ADE$ arises from triangle $ABC$ by a rotation of $90^\circ$ about the point $A$. If angle $D$ is $60^\circ$ and angle $E$ is $40^\circ$, how large is the angle $v$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2009_p1_fig.png
Solve the system of equations $$\frac{1}{x+y} + x = 3, \qquad \frac{x}{x+y} = 2.$$

For a party, Georg has bought lots of filled chocolates, and when he counts how many he has, he finds that the number is a prime. He distributes as many of the chocolates as possible onto $60$ plates with the same number on each. He then notes that he has more than one piece left over, and that the number of leftover pieces is not a prime.

How many pieces of chocolate does Georg have left over?

Let $E$ be an arbitrary point, different from $A$ and $B$, on the side $AB$ of a square $ABCD$, and let $F$ and $G$ be points on the segment $CE$ such that $BF$ and $DG$ are perpendicular to $CE$.

Prove that $|DF| = |AG|$.

Imagine a square array consisting of $n \times n$ fields with side length $1$, where $n$ is an arbitrary positive integer. What is the largest possible length of a route you can follow along the edges of the fields from the point $A$ in the lower left corner to the point $B$ in the upper right corner, if you may never return to a point where you have been before? (The figure shows, for $n = 5$, an example of an allowed route (left) and an example of a route that is not allowed (right).)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2009_p5_fig.png

Four right triangles, each with legs $1$ and $2$, are put together into a figure as shown.

What fraction of the area of the large circle is the area of the small circle?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2010_p1_fig.png
Prove that for every integer $n$ there exist integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ such that $n = a^2 + b^2 - c^2$.
Can $29$ boys and $31$ girls be lined up in a row, holding hands, so that nobody holds hands with two girls?

An equilateral triangle $ABC$ is given. A semicircle with $BC$ as diameter is drawn outside the triangle. Points $D$ and $E$ are chosen on the semicircle such that the arcs $BD$, $DE$ and $EC$ have equal lengths.

Prove that the segments $AD$ and $AE$ divide the side $BC$ into three equal parts.

It is given that $2^{2010}$ is a $606$-digit number beginning with $1$.

How many of the numbers $1, 2, 2^2, 2^3, \dots, 2^{2009}$ begin with $4$?

Georg writes the numbers from $1$ to $15$ on separate pieces of paper. He tries to place the pieces of paper in two piles so that neither pile contains two numbers whose sum is a perfect square.

Prove that it cannot be done.

(The perfect squares are the numbers $0 = 0^2$, $1 = 1^2$, $4 = 2^2$, $9 = 3^2$, etc.)

In the octagon shown below, all sides have length $1$ and all angles are equal.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2011_p2_fig.png

Determine the distance between the vertices $A$ and $B$.
Determine all the ways in which the fraction $\frac{1}{11}$ can be written as $\frac{1}{n} + \frac{1}{m}$, where $n$ and $m$ are two distinct positive integers.
A function $f$ is given by $$f(x) = x^2 - 2x.$$ Prove that there exists a number $a$ satisfying $f(f(a)) = a$ without $f(a) = a$.
Determine all triples $(a, b, c)$ of positive integers such that $b^2$ is obtained by removing the last digit of $c^2$, and $a^2$ is obtained by removing the last digit of $b^2$.

Inside a circle with radius $6$ lie four smaller circles with centres $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$. The circles touch each other as shown. The point where the circles with centres $A$ and $C$ touch each other is the centre of the large circle.

Compute the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2012_p1_fig.png

About a rectangle it is given that it can be divided into nine squares placed relative to each other as shown. The black square has side length $1$.

Is there more than one possibility for the side lengths of the rectangle?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/denmark_2012_p2_fig.png

Georg wants to put his $250$ stamps into a new album. On the first page he puts one stamp, and then on each page either the same number or twice as many as on the previous page. In this way he ends up having put exactly all $250$ stamps into the album.

What is the smallest number of pages he can manage with?

Two two-digit numbers $a$ and $b$ satisfy that the product $a \cdot b$ divides the four-digit number obtained by writing the two digits of $a$ followed by the two digits of $b$.

Determine all possible values of $a$ and $b$.

In a hexagon $ABCDEF$ all angles are equal. The side lengths satisfy $|AB| = |CD| = |EF| = 3$ and $|BC| = |DE| = |FA| = 2$. The diagonals $AD$ and $CF$ intersect at the point $G$. The point $H$ lies on the side $CD$ such that $|DH| = 1$.

Prove that triangle $EGH$ is equilateral.

Georg plays the following game. He chooses two positive integers $n$ and $k$. On an $n \times n$ board where all the fields are white, Georg paints $k$ of the fields black. Then he counts how many black fields there are in each row, takes the square of each of these $n$ numbers and adds the squares. He calls the result $S$. In the same way he counts the number of white fields in each row, takes the square of each of these $n$ numbers and adds the squares. He calls the result $H$. Georg would like to achieve $S - H = 49$.

Determine all values of $n$ and $k$ for which this is possible.

Example: If Georg chooses $n = 5$ and $k = 14$, he can, for example, paint the board as shown. Then $$S = 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + 3^2 + 5^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 + 9 + 25 = 48,$$ $$H = 4^2 + 3^2 + 2^2 + 2^2 + 0^2 = 16 + 9 + 4 + 4 + 0 = 33,$$ so here $S - H = 48 - 33 = 15$.
